title: Modulus functions
examples: How is the graph of the modulus function different from a normal function?
Can you show me how to solve an inequality involving the modulus function?
What happens to the graph when the expression inside the modulus is negative?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the modulus function. It is often written using vertical bars like this. We say this is the modulus of a number.
The modulus of a number is its distance from zero on the number line. Distance is always a positive value or zero. So the result is never negative.
Let us look at a simple example. The modulus of five is simply five. The distance of five from zero is five.
Now consider the modulus of negative three. The distance of negative three from zero is three. So we write this as three.
This means that for any number x, the modulus function always gives you the positive version of that number. This creates a V shape when we graph it.

faq.q: What is the difference between the modulus function and the absolute value?
faq.a: They are the same thing. The absolute value bars are just a different way to write the modulus function. You can use either one.
asks: Is modulus the same as absolute value?

faq.q: How do I graph the modulus function if the expression is more complex?
faq.a: You graph the inner function first, and then you take the absolute value of every y coordinate. This means any negative y value becomes positive.
asks: What do I do if the graph goes below the x-axis?

faq.q: When solving an equation like |2x - 1| = 5, what steps should I take?
faq.a: You must set up two separate equations. One assuming the inside is positive, and one assuming the inside is negative. You solve both cases.
asks: Do I solve one equation or two?

faq.q: What happens if I have an inequality like |x| < 3?
faq.a: This means the distance of x from zero must be less than three. This results in a range between negative three and positive three.
asks: How do I solve an inequality with modulus?

faq.a: Yes, you can. You follow the same method as before. You set up two separate equations to solve for x.
asks: Is solving modulus equations always two parts?

facts: The modulus of a number is its distance from zero.
The modulus function always outputs a non-negative result.
If |a| = b, then a = b or a = -b.
Graphing |x| results in a V-shaped graph.

quiz.why: The distance of negative ten from zero is ten, so the modulus is ten.

wrong.0: This is tempting if you multiply the numbers inside the bars.
wrong.1: This is tempting if you think the modulus always results in zero.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might forget to take the absolute value.

quiz.say: If |x| = 7, what are two possible values for x?
quiz.why: The distance from zero must be seven, so x could be positive seven or negative seven.

wrong.0: This is tempting if you multiply the number by two.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because the modulus of zero is zero, not seven.
wrong.3: This is only one possible answer, but the modulus allows for two.

quiz.say: What is the solution set for the inequality |x - 2| <= 3?
quiz.why: This inequality means the distance between x and 2 is at most 3. This gives the range from -1 to 5.

wrong.0: This incorrectly assumes the inequality must be solved by subtracting 3 from the inside.
wrong.1: This only solves the case where (x-2) is positive, ignoring the negative case.
wrong.2: This treats the inequality like an equation, finding only the endpoints.
